# MAG 7 Daily
> **After 16,000-plus paper checks, Google opens Deep Review publicly.**

**What You Need to Know:** Google Research has opened Deep Review to the public after private checks on more than 16,000 manuscripts. New iPhone Duo orders have slipped into early 2027 after Apple called demand extraordinary. Microsoft shipped a legal edition of Copilot, and Apple tightened App Store rules on AI intimate imagery.

### Top News
**Deep Review opens after conference pilots on more than 16,000 manuscripts: Google Research**
Rajesh Jayaram and Vincent Cohen-Addad of Google Research say Deep Review, the public successor to the Paper Assistant Tool, is now available worldwide after opted-in authors received private pre-submission feedback on more than 16,000 manuscripts at STOC 2026, ICML 2026, NeurIPS 2026, and ICLR 2027. The system checks logical consistency and mathematical statements, suggests improvements, grounds facts, and compares a document with existing work. Inputs are PDFs and plain text at launch, with multi-file inputs coming soon. Users who need more than the free tier can attach a Gemini API key for higher limits and for the Deep Review API. Uploaded documents are never used to train, fine-tune, or improve Google models. Further detail on the pilots is in the manuscript Towards Automating Scientific Review with Google’s Paper Assistant Tool. Source: [research.google](https://research.google/blog/analyzing-technical-documents-with-deep-review/)

**Apple calls iPhone Duo demand extraordinary as new orders slip into 2027: MacRumors**
Apple told the Financial Times that demand has been “nothing short of extraordinary” and that it is “working hard to get this revolutionary new product into customers’ hands as quickly as possible.” Pre-orders opened at 5:00 a.m. Pacific on October 16; within minutes delivery dates slipped from October 23 to November, and by 5:30 a.m. estimates reached January 25. It is no longer possible to order an iPhone Duo from Apple for delivery in 2026, so buyers now wait until early 2027, while the first orders are still set for delivery on October 23. Pricing starts at 1,999 dollars and goes to 3,199 dollars for 2TB; the Financial Times described deliveries of the 2,000-dollar Duo slipping to 2027 within hours of going on sale. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/16/apple-iphone-duo-demand-extraordinary/) · [ft.com](https://www.ft.com/content/7b236286-ca1d-4063-a728-7f968a638b8f?syn-25a6b1a6=1)

**Microsoft launches Copilot for Legal with more than 20 skills: KuCoin**
On October 16, Microsoft President and Vice Chairman Brad Smith announced Copilot for Legal, with more than 20 specialized AI skills for commercial customers worldwide, built as legal plugins inside Copilot. Each skill maps to a task such as drafting contracts, reviewing agreements, tracking obligations, or organizing case timelines. Microsoft’s blog says those capabilities sit mainly in desktop Word and in Cowork, which can pull obligations, deadlines, and trigger conditions from contracts, emails, minutes, and documents, compare terms across agreements, build case timelines, or turn a meeting into minutes and resolutions. Partner plugins named in the launch include Bloomberg Law, Thomson Reuters HighQ, DocuSign, Harvey, Relativity, iManage, and NetDocuments, covering legal research, document management, e-signatures, e-discovery, and transaction management. Plugins roll out gradually through the Microsoft Plugin Registry, and availability can vary by region, licensing, and administrator settings. Microsoft says the tool assists lawyers and does not replace legal judgment, so citations, conclusions, and revision suggestions still need manual checks, and an enterprise needs a commercial Microsoft 365 Copilot license plus a supported Word setup. Source: [kucoin.com](https://www.kucoin.com/news/flash/microsoft-launches-legal-version-of-copilot-with-over-20-ai-legal-skills)

**App Store rules now target AI nudify apps and hidden features: MacRumors**
Apple expanded App Store rules to cover AI-generated nonconsensual intimate imagery. Sexually explicit content was already banned; developers must now proactively prevent and remove AI deepfakes, and apps can be removed if they do not. Updated guideline 1.2 names AI content-creation apps. New guideline 2.5.19 says features that were not in the version submitted for review can mean removal from the App Store and the Apple Developer Program, aimed at “nudification” apps that hid that function until after approval. Section 5’s ban on apps that facilitate human trafficking or child exploitation now also covers alternative app distribution. MacRumors reports that earlier this year Apple told xAI it would remove Grok if nude deepfakes continued, xAI added safeguards, and Apple approved an updated app. The Verge reports that Apple did not pull X or Grok, after criticism that X users had used Grok to make nonconsensual sexualized deepfakes, including of minors. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/16/app-store-rules-deepfakes/) · [theverge.com](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1013314/apple-app-store-nudify-ai-apps-harassment)

### Company Desk
**Former AWS engineer says Bee’s consent cues miss bystanders: GeekWire**
Jeff Williams, a former AWS security engineer and now chief information security officer at Sigma360, told GeekWire that the consent prompt and indicator light on Amazon’s Bee Frontier and Bee Eclipse reach the wearer, not the people being recorded. Amazon pointed to safeguards that include automatic shutoff and reminders for users to ask permission. Source: [geekwire.com](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/amazons-new-bee-ai-devices-have-a-bystander-problem-says-former-aws-security-engineer/)

### The Counterpoint
**Two free reviews a week against 74,000 submissions, and the official verdict stays human: Google Research**
Deep Review does not enter the official peer-review decision. Google Research says this year’s submissions to ICLR, NeurIPS, and ICML topped 74,000, up from about 45,000 in 2025, 32,000 in 2024, and 23,000 in 2023, while every user gets two complimentary document reviews a week. In the conference pilots, feedback was completely decoupled from the official review, and papers were deleted from Google systems promptly after each program; the public product stores uploads for one year so the user can see them in the Deep Review interface. The system is built to take on consistency checks and leave higher-level judgements to humans. Source: [research.google](https://research.google/blog/analyzing-technical-documents-with-deep-review/)

### The Thread: One UK gateway, three of the seven
In May 2026, the U.K. Competition and Markets Authority opened an investigation into whether Microsoft should be designated as having Strategic Market Status in its business software ecosystem. On October 16, 2026, the authority proposed that designation. The CMA says Strategic Market Status does not find or assume wrongdoing. It is a gateway into the country’s digital markets competition regime, and it could lead to measures that affect how Microsoft bundles Excel, Teams, and Copilot.

Alphabet is already inside the same regime. Last year the CMA designated Google with Strategic Market Status in general search and advertising services after confirming that the company met the legal criteria. Amazon sits in the adjacent file. In March the regulator began consulting stakeholders on whether Amazon Web Services and Microsoft were following through on commitments to improve customer choice in cloud services, and on whether further action was necessary. Friday’s proposal stacks workplace software and Copilot onto a cloud check that already names Amazon and Microsoft, and onto a search designation that already names Google.

The CMA says Microsoft has held a dominant position in U.K. business software for decades, first through operating systems and productivity tools, then cybersecurity and database management, with AI products and cloud services now adding further reach. U.K. businesses and public-sector organizations can benefit from buying several digital products from Microsoft, and they may also face barriers when they try to switch. The products are closely integrated, which the authority says offers a more seamless experience than combining services from different companies. Control over key APIs, technical interfaces, and data flows can make it harder for competing providers to deliver the same functionality.

The examination the CMA described is about choice, not a penalty already imposed. It will look at whether customers can choose their preferred AI tools and whether competing providers can compete effectively with Copilot. It will assess whether bundling of security products restricted customer choice, and how licensing practices affected cloud options. Sarah Cardell, chief executive of the CMA, said organizations should be able to choose the products that work best for them, switch provider when they want to, and combine services from different suppliers. A Microsoft spokesperson told Reuters that the company’s products, including Copilot, are “open and interoperable, giving customers the ability to use them alongside competing services.” Microsoft did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comment.

Benzinga wrote that analysts highlight 30 million Copilot seats, Azure momentum, and Maia 300 inference chips ahead of fiscal Q1 2027 earnings. That seat figure is an analyst highlight in the piece, not a number Microsoft stated to the CMA. Comments on the proposed decision are invited by November 13, and the authority will take a final decision by February 13, 2027. Source: [benzinga.com](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/tech/26/10/62427164/uk-watchdog-microsoft-competition-scrutiny)

### On the Calendar
Apple’s October 15, 2026 Newsroom release says iPhone Duo availability begins on October 30, 2026. Source: [ad-hoc-news.de](https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/apple-announces-iphone-duo-preorders-what-it-means-for-apple-stock/70346576)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **Two firms, Amazon and Microsoft, can still ease UK cloud switching.**

**What You Need to Know:** The UK Competition and Markets Authority says Amazon Web Services and Microsoft can do more to remove barriers that still make it hard to switch cloud providers or to use several clouds at once. The authority is still weighing whether to open a full investigation into strategic market status in the UK cloud market. Elsewhere, Google locked a 2027 cockpit deal with Geely, British Airways wrote Meta’s glasses into its carriage rules, and Gemini 4 Argon reached Antigravity.

### Top News
**UK watchdog says Amazon and Microsoft can still ease cloud switching: UA.NEWS**
The UK Competition and Markets Authority said Amazon Web Services and Microsoft can do more to remove barriers that still make it difficult to switch cloud providers. The same assessment covers using several cloud services rather than one. The authority said clearing those obstacles should expand choice for customers in the United Kingdom. It also said it will keep considering whether to launch a full investigation into strategic market status in the UK cloud-services market. Source: [ua.news](https://ua.news/en/it-ta-telekom/britanskii-reguliator-zaiaviv-shcho-aws-i-microsoft-mozhut-usunuti-barieri-channel-newsasia) Source: [tradingview.com](https://www.tradingview.com/news/reuters.com,2026:newsml_P8N3OV050:0-uk-s-cma-says-more-can-be-done-by-aws-microsoft-to-address-remaining-barriers-in-cloud-services/)

**Geely puts Gemini, Maps and Play on overseas cars from late 2027: CarNewsChina**
On October 16, Geely Holding Group said it had established a global partnership with Google for a digital-cockpit ecosystem on Geely passenger-vehicle brands in overseas markets where Google services are available. Chief technology officer Dr. Shen Yuan said the first model with those services reaches the global market in the second half of 2027. On the cars, Gemini, Maps and Play are meant to cover destinations, nearby charging stations, apps and other routine tasks, including voice commands. Shen said the point is not more technology in front of the driver: “A digital cockpit can become crowded very quickly.” The holding company’s brands include Geely, Geely Galaxy, Zeekr, Lynk & Co, Volvo, Polestar, Lotus, Smart, Farizon, Proton, LEVC and Riddara. Zeekr had already paired with AirConsole for in-car cloud gaming, and in April 2026 Zeekr signed with 3 Screen Solutions to build a media platform on Android Automotive OS. Source: [carnewschina.com](https://carnewschina.com/2026/10/16/geely-cars-to-get-google-gemini-maps-and-play-globally-in-h2-2027/) Source: [asiabusinessoutlook.com](https://www.asiabusinessoutlook.com/news/geely-to-bring-google-gemini-and-maps-to-overseas-cars-in-2027-nwid-12631.html)

**British Airways writes Meta AI glasses into its filming ban: PYOK**
British Airways amended its General Conditions of Carriage so passengers may not use Meta AI glasses to covertly film staff or fellow seatmates. Section 7A.10 lets the airline refuse carriage for filming, live-streaming or photographing BA crew or other colleagues without consent, folded into harassment and abusive-conduct grounds. Section 11A lets the airline make a passenger leave the aircraft, refuse another flight including a pre-booked return, and report the passenger to the police for filming crew without consent. Passengers may still wear the glasses; an LED is meant to show recording, and PYOK notes reports of wearers covering that light. Cabin crew and other customer-facing BA workers are already banned from using smart glasses. The change follows, by months, a ban on photographing or filming those workers without express consent, and on live-streaming anyone without permission. In June, Volotea ground staff at Oviedo refused to engage a travel vlogger who would not stop recording a service exchange in Meta AI glasses; the airline’s reply warned that the conduct potentially breached Spanish privacy laws. Source: [paddleyourownkanoo.com](https://www.paddleyourownkanoo.com/2026/10/16/british-airways-bans-passengers-from-using-meta-ai-glasses-on-board-its-aircraft/)

**Gemini 4 Argon is live in Antigravity for paid subscribers: 9to5Google**
Google is rolling Gemini 4 Argon into Antigravity, its agentic coding tool, for AI Pro and AI Ultra subscribers, after a wider rollout to users earlier this week. A separate weekly-only Argon quota sits on top of the existing quota for Gemini 3.8 Flash. Google says Argon is designed to tackle the hardest problems. On YouTube’s comments frontend, Argon traced production profiles, found redundant emoji rendering at nearly 45 percent of server overhead, and drove 12 optimizations that cut the CPU footprint in half, cut server comment-load latency by 30 milliseconds and cut client end-to-end latency by 20 milliseconds. On an on-call bug queue of 134 open reports, agents closed 97 stale or duplicate tickets in under 3 hours, a 72.4 percent reduction, and left 37 sorted by owner. Auditing a batch of access-control changes, Argon found four critical security bugs after two earlier frontier models had reported zero on the same code. A Fortran-to-Rust rewrite through a custom skill delivered a 1.8-times performance boost, and an Ads sales workflow cut prospect research time by 90 percent, about 10 hours a week. Source: [9to5google.com](https://9to5google.com/2026/10/15/gemini-4-argon-is-now-rolling-out-to-googles-antigravity-for-ai-pro-subscribers/)

### Company Desk
**Apple’s store is down as iPhone Duo pre-orders open: MacRumors**
Apple took the online store offline ahead of iPhone Duo pre-orders, which begin at 5:00 a.m. Pacific Time on October 16. The US store message reads: “We love that early energy. Almost ready for you. Pre-order begins at 5:00 a.m. PT. See you soon.” Customers in more than 70 countries and regions, including Australia, Canada, China, France, Germany, India, Japan, Mexico, the UAE, the UK and the US, can pre-order when the store returns. The foldable comes in Star White and Night Sky, in 256GB, 512GB, 1TB and 2TB. In the United States it starts at 1,999. Apple has opened pre-orders at 5:00 a.m. Pacific for several years, rather than the old 12:01 a.m. start. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/10/16/apple-store-down-ahead-of-iphone-duo-pre-orders/)

### The Counterpoint
**The cloud step is still a decision to keep considering: UA.NEWS**
Against the warning to Amazon and Microsoft, today’s statements do not open the case. The Competition and Markets Authority said it will continue considering whether to launch a full investigation into strategic market status in UK cloud services. That yes-or-no on a strategic-market-status investigation is the decision that would turn a public nudge into a formal market probe. Source: [ua.news](https://ua.news/en/it-ta-telekom/britanskii-reguliator-zaiaviv-shcho-aws-i-microsoft-mozhut-usunuti-barieri-channel-newsasia)

### The Thread: A tenth of a second on two laptops’ chips
Amazon Web Services put a two-billion-parameter decision model in the open, and the only speed numbers it published were measured on an NVIDIA graphics card and an Apple laptop chip. Strands Decider 2B is built to pick among choices a developer already listed — model routing, tool selection, classification, guardrails, context management — and to return a decision with confidence scores instead of a long generated answer. The base is Qwen3.5-2B. AWS replaced the language-model head with a pointer head that scores candidate answers, then fine-tuned with a rank-16 LoRA adapter. Weights, training data and scripts are out, so a developer can run and change the model locally through the strands-decider package, on the command line or inside Strands agents.

The clock AWS cites is short. Median decision latency was about 115 milliseconds on an NVIDIA RTX 3090. Small tasks took 153 milliseconds on an Apple M3 MacBook. On JevBench, the v19 checkpoint scored 72.3 percent accuracy across 231 public tasks. Those two machines are not AWS products. They are the hardware a developer already has on a desk: an NVIDIA consumer GPU in one test, an Apple silicon laptop in the other. The model’s job is to sit in front of a larger system and choose a tool or a route. If that choice takes a tenth of a second on a 3090 and about a sixth of a second on an M3, the wait is in the same band as a sluggish click, not a cloud round trip the article never claims to have measured.

InfoQ places Decider against TypeSafe AI’s Jev, another model aimed at structured decisions, classification, routing and tool selection, also returning confidence scores. The split InfoQ draws is deployment, not a winner on the benchmark: Decider is open source and can run locally; Jev is a managed API. AWS evaluated Decider on JevBench. The published results, InfoQ says, do not establish a direct performance advantage over Jev. So the 72.3 percent figure is a score on 231 tasks for one checkpoint, not a claim that Amazon beat the specialist it borrowed a bench from.

The same announcement pairs the small model with Strands Box, in developer preview, as the execution cage around whatever model is chosen. Box combines operating-system isolation with Dogwood, an open-source policy language, and routes shell commands, Python, MCP tools, filesystem operations and network access through a policy layer outside the language model. A rule can require tests before a push, cap how often an agent calls an external API, or block outbound HTTP after the agent reads a customer file. AWS says Box can sit on different models and agent frameworks, local or in the cloud. NVIDIA and Apple do not ship that policy layer. They show up because the decision step was timed on their silicon, and because GitHub discussion already flags Apple Silicon compatibility, concurrent requests and cold-start latency as problems to check before production. AWS Community Builder Yuuki Yamashita, in a hands-on tutorial, reported that Decider 2B could stop an agent from making an unsupported weather-tool call.

What changes is where the choice is made. Amazon is offering a two-billion-parameter pointer model that developers can fine-tune and run beside the NVIDIA and Apple hardware they already own, then wrap the chosen action in a kernel policy instead of a prompt. The numbers that decide whether that is faster than calling a managed decider are the ones AWS printed: 115 milliseconds, 153 milliseconds, 72.3 percent on 231 tasks, rank-16 on a Qwen3.5-2B base, and no published head-to-head win over Jev.

# MAG 7 Daily
> **House House is keeping August's Big Walk off Xbox over Microsoft's Israel ties.**

**What You Need to Know:** House House is keeping its August co-op, Big Walk, off Xbox, citing Microsoft's involvement with Israel. Tim Cook now says Apple Intelligence is approved in China, with a test version later this month and no AI Siri in the first batch. Google is also putting Gemini on unknown-sender texts in Android Messages, while scammers keep walking people toward WhatsApp.

### Top News
**House House keeps Big Walk off Xbox over Microsoft and Israel: The Verge**
House House is not shipping Big Walk, its co-op multiplayer walking adventure, on Xbox consoles. The Verge reports the game has proved popular since it launched in August, and Xbox players have been left out. The studio said in a blog post that it decided against an Xbox release in line with a Palestinian-led boycott of Microsoft's involvement with Israel. Source: [theverge.com](https://www.theverge.com/games/1011785/big-walk-house-house-microsoft-xbox-bds-boycott)

**Cook says Apple Intelligence is approved in China; Siri AI waits: The News International**
After years of regulatory delay, Tim Cook told The Paper, in a Thursday interview in Shanghai, that Apple Intelligence has been approved in China. A test version is expected later in October. He said the first batch covers writing tools, real-time translation and image cleanup, and he ruled out AI-powered Siri in that first introduction. Reuters carried the same account from The Paper. The same day in Beijing, Commerce Minister Wang Wentao met Cook; a Ministry of Commerce statement says Cook told Wang that Apple is optimistic about China's prospects and will further expand its operations there. Wang said he hopes Apple will act as a communication bridge on China-US trade and on AI that is safe, controllable and governed through cooperation. TechNode, separately, reports that Apple plans a December China launch using Alibaba models. Source: [thenews.com.pk](https://www.thenews.com.pk/latest/1420016-tim-cook-announces-major-apple-intelligence-update-for-china) · [reuters.com](https://www.reuters.com/business/retail-consumer/tim-cook-says-apple-intelligence-approved-china-paper-reports-2026-10-15/) · [finance.biggo.com](https://finance.biggo.com/news/b2cb5d23-362b-47d9-a3f4-33bd309ee48b) · [technode.com](https://technode.com/2026/10/15/apple-reportedly-plans-december-china-launch-for-apple-intelligence-using-alibaba-models/)

**A writer pulls a 118-row Amazon file after Alexa names the dog: Business Insider**
A Business Insider writer says Alexa suddenly knew the dog's name, and then downloaded the Amazon dossier on that account. The file ran to 118 rows. Source: [businessinsider.com](https://www.businessinsider.com/what-does-amazon-alexa-know-about-me-dogs-name-2026-10)

### Company Desk
**Google sets AI collaborations and funding for health and research in India: The Times of India**
Google is announcing AI collaborations and funding initiatives aimed at healthcare and research in India. The Times of India reported the move on October 15. Source: [timesofindia.indiatimes.com](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/technology/tech-news/google-announces-ai-collaborations-funding-initiatives-to-boost-healthcare-research-in-india/articleshow/134963544.cms)

**NVIDIA widens technology access for Europe's scientific community: NVIDIA Blog**
NVIDIA says it is expanding advanced technology access for Europe's scientific community. The routes it names are open learning resources, collaborations and compute. Source: [blogs.nvidia.com](https://blogs.nvidia.com/blog/ec-scientific-computing-pledge/)

### The Counterpoint
**One popular August game is off Xbox; Microsoft's own operations are not what the post changes: The Verge**
The boycott, as The Verge has it, is a studio decision about one title, not a Microsoft filing, remedy or product withdrawal. Big Walk has been popular since August, so the people who lose the game are Xbox players of a title that already found an audience elsewhere. What would decide whether this is a platform problem or a single credits-screen choice is whether other studios follow House House. This report names one game and one blog post. Source: [theverge.com](https://www.theverge.com/games/1011785/big-walk-house-house-microsoft-xbox-bds-boycott)

### The Thread: The text leaves Google's phone
Google is turning Gemini loose on scam texts, and the handoff the researchers describe runs straight out of Google Messages toward WhatsApp. The Neuron says Google is expanding Gemini-powered scam detection in Android's Messages app with an opt-in mode called Enhanced Protection, rolling out over the coming weeks. When a number that is not in your contacts texts you, cloud-based Gemini models can read the conversation and judge whether it is a scam. Notebookcheck, citing Google's October 14 post, says those chats go to cloud Gemini models meant to read the wider context, which is the point for slow-burn fraud that asks for money only after a long run of harmless messages. Google says the analysis happens in Private AI Compute, where data is encrypted and processed in a secure dedicated space and stays inaccessible to anyone else, including Google. The Neuron says it could not verify the privacy claim.

A second layer stays on the phone. Gemini Nano checks unfamiliar links against real-time web signals before a tap. Google limits that check to the Pixel 10 and newer Pixels, the Galaxy S26 series, the Galaxy Z Fold8, the Galaxy Z Flip8 and other select devices. Redesigned warnings for links from numbers outside your contacts reach further: Android 6 and later. They warn. They do not block. The final tap is still the user's. Coverage is only unknown senders.

The numbers around the problem are larger than one settings toggle. A University of Florida study of 175,430 user-reported scam texts found that link-based scams, such as fake toll and postal notices, reuse near-identical scripts and are easier to filter. Reply-based scams, including romance and wrong-number texts, adapt to each victim and grew much faster. A wrong-number text with no link gives a keyword filter nothing to catch. Text scam losses reported to the FTC in 2024 were $470 million at minimum. Total reported fraud losses in 2025 were $15.9 billion, a record, and texting was the top reported contact method. In a Google-released 2025 survey of users in the US, India and Brazil, Android users were 58 percent likelier to report zero scam texts in a week. That figure is self-reported. Google says Scam Detection in Phone by Google and Google Messages already flags more than 5 million suspected scam calls and texts every month. Notebookcheck notes that figure comes from Google and has not been checked independently. In the Florida team's test of general chatbots, GPT-5 missed 18.8 percent of scams.

The shared limit is the next app. The Florida study, as The Neuron reports it, found scammers often move victims to WhatsApp or Telegram. Enhanced Protection does not follow that move. Meta's messaging app is where a Google warning can end and a fresh chat can start, with no Gemini read of the thread the user was just talked into opening. That is the platform dependency: Google can screen an unknown sender inside Messages, and the scam's design is to leave Messages.

The rest of the package is dated, and it is still Google's stack. Chrome and Android WebView will hide login fields and payment screens during screen sharing, rolling out in October to devices on Android 15 and later. Android will block apps from switching on call forwarding in the background, and it will warn before a forwarding code takes effect if a caller talks someone into typing it. That starts in early December on Pixel phones and other select devices. Scam alerts in the notifications of popular chat apps have been a Pixel feature; Google plans to bring them to Motorola, OnePlus, Oppo, Xiaomi, Vivo, Honor and other phone makers later this year. Reporting a text as spam still sends the message and its contents to Google, and that step is optional, on the Pixel 6 and later and on the Galaxy S24 series and later. The setting that reads unknown-sender chats is opt-in. Leaving it off keeps the older on-device detection. Source: [theneurondaily.com](https://www.theneurondaily.com/p/gemini-now-screens-scam-texts) · [notebookcheck.net](https://www.notebookcheck.net/Google-Messages-Gemini-will-soon-screen-texts-from-unknown-senders.1424963.0.html)

### Top News
**An 8.1 bug in AWS sample code let denied callers run privileged calls: shattered.io**
AWS patched a privilege-escalation flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-94384 and scored 8.1, in the sfExecuteAWSService function inside the AmazonConnectSalesforceLambda application. That app is the glue between Amazon Connect contact centers and Salesforce Service Cloud Voice. The function accepted caller-supplied parameters for which AWS operation to run, then executed that operation with its own privileged role without checking whether the invoking identity was allowed to do it. The only permission required was lambda:InvokeFunction. From there the function's role could run API calls the caller's own policy explicitly denied, which the write-up calls an IAM identity bypass and a confused-deputy problem. # MAG 7 Daily
> **One unpatched key lets local Mac software hijack Meta's Muse assistant.**

**What You Need to Know:** One unpatched key lets local Mac software hijack Meta's Muse assistant, and the desktop client will send dictation audio plus the account token to whatever server that key names. SandboxAQ's potency model is now on the AWS Marketplace for North American commercial customers, and Meta-backed Eliyan is drawing takeover interest over AI data-transfer bottlenecks. Google is testing a Gemini 4 coding checkpoint called Carbon on an internal platform.

### Top News
**Unpatched Muse key lets local Mac software redirect dictation: 36Kr**
Patrick Wardle, founder of the Objective-See Foundation, has disclosed an unpatched flaw in Meta's new Muse macOS client, 36Kr reports. Software running as an ordinary user can overwrite an undocumented preference, endo_voyager_dictation_endpoint, without an administrator password or a macOS authorization prompt. That key names the server that receives dictation audio and returns the transcript. Change it, and the client sends raw microphone audio and the Muse account's authentication token to an endpoint the attacker controls. Wardle ran a proxy that forwarded traffic on to Meta while keeping the token and the audio. With the session, hidden instructions can be added to voice requests so the assistant acts in the background, including taking local documents or WhatsApp message records. Mark Zuckerberg had said the assistant was built with privacy and security at its core from the start. Source: [eu.36kr.com](https://eu.36kr.com/en/p/4019730918363011)

**SandboxAQ's AQPotency opens on the AWS Marketplace: Quantum Zeitgeist**
SandboxAQ's AQPotency is available to AWS commercial customers in North America through the AWS Marketplace, and it deploys as an Amazon SageMaker model package. It predicts how strongly a candidate compound binds a protein from a UniProt ID and a ligand SMILES string, with no 3D crystal structure, which brings in targets such as membrane proteins, mutant panels, and proteins that have not been crystallized. Teams can rank millions of compounds in a few hours on standard CPU instances inside their own AWS environment, through a real-time endpoint or large asynchronous jobs. SandboxAQ says it collects no metadata on users' targets or molecules. The model has also been reachable through Claude via the Model Context Protocol since August. Source: [quantumzeitgeist.com](https://quantumzeitgeist.com/aqpotency-available-aws-customers-north/)

**Meta-backed Eliyan draws takeover interest over AI data links: The Information**
Eliyan, backed by AMD, Cisco, and Meta, is drawing takeover interest, The Information reports. The interest is tied to data-transfer bottlenecks that are slowing AI systems. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/newsletters/dealmaker/networking-startup-eliyan-draws-takeover-interest-held-early-talks-arm?utm_campaign=Editorial&utm_content=Article&utm_medium=organic_social&utm_source=bluesky,threads,twitter)

**Google tests Gemini 4 Carbon on internal coding: The Decoder**
Google has put a Gemini 4 checkpoint called Carbon on its internal coding platform Jetski over the past few days, where it is said to beat still-unshipped Argon mainly on programming tasks, The Decoder reports from documents, screenshots, and internal chats Business Insider reviewed. One employee compared Carbon to Anthropic's Opus 5.5 and said it still needs more testing; early Argon builds reminded another employee of the older Opus 5 on some coding tasks. Google's own map calls Argon the frontier reasoning model, Flash the speed-and-volume model, Omni the generative-media model, and Gemma the lightweight open-weights edge model. Carbon and Barium read as checkpoints inside the Argon family: an employee called Carbon "Gemini pro next model," and internal documents had labeled the now-unveiled Argon as "Barium-B." DeepMind's Vedant Misra replied on X, "Have you heard of recursive self improvement." There is still no official Gemini 4 launch date. Logan Kilpatrick has confirmed the team is working on getting the most out of Argon. Source: [the-decoder.com](https://the-decoder.com/googles-gemini-4-carbon-model-is-reportedly-matching-anthropics-opus-5-5-coding-performance/)

### The Counterpoint
**The Muse hijack still needs software already on the Mac, and dictation switched on: 36Kr**
Wardle's path is not a remote break-in by itself. The rewrite is open to unprivileged local processes and arbitrary scripts already running as the user, and the microphone audio and token leave only when dictation is enabled. Meta has not issued a security advisory, the flaw has no CVE ID, and the open question is whether that preference stays writable before a patch lands. Source: [eu.36kr.com](https://eu.36kr.com/en/p/4019730918363011)

### The Thread: Three home platforms, seven bulbs
A roundup of seven smart bulbs treats Alexa, Google Home, and Apple Home as the test a lamp has to pass. Geeky Gadgets, drawing on a Smart Home 101 breakdown, highlights the ABRA bulb at a color rendering index of 90, with tunable white from 2700K to 6500K. ABRA comes as an A19 rated at 800 lumens and a BR30 rated at 750 lumens, and the write-up says it works with Alexa, Google Home, and Siri without a hub. LIFX is the brightness and wide-color option, also hub-free. Philips Hue is the customization lane: Chroma Sync, plus an optional Hue Bridge when the three voice platforms are not enough control. Govee is listed for music sync, 16 million colors, and 54 preset scenes. The Amazon Basics bulb is described as streamlined Alexa integration, not as the lamp built to treat Google and Apple the same way. Third Reality's ZL1 is the Zigbee bulb, a mesh radio aimed at network reliability instead of depending only on the Wi-Fi path those assistants usually use. Alphabet, Amazon, and Apple are not the lamp makers in this comparison. They are the compatibility gate. A bulb that misses one assistant drops out of a list organized around exactly those three. The spec that splits the field is the hub. ABRA, LIFX, and the Basics path are sold as hub-free. Hue's bridge is optional, and the breakdown calls that bridge the route to maximum control. Zigbee on the ZL1 is the pitch when a Wi-Fi link to an assistant is the failure point. Three of the seven set the checkbox. The bulb makers spend lumens, color counts, and radio choices proving they clear it. Source: [geeky-gadgets.com](https://www.geeky-gadgets.com/best-smart-bulb-2026/)

> **180 billion watermarked images are now checkable by the public through Google's SynthID Detector.**

**What You Need to Know:** Google has released SynthID Detector so the public can check watermarks the company says already sit on more than 180 billion images and videos. Amazon's Strands Box, out in developer preview, lets a policy limit an agent's next move based on what it already did. Alphabet's Isomorphic Labs is in early talks to raise funds at a valuation of at least $40 billion.

### Top News
**Google releases new AI detection tool: The Independent**
Google has released SynthID Detector so people can check whether text, image, audio, or video was made with AI, The Independent reports. The check reads imperceptible watermarks Google says it has already applied to more than 180 billion images and videos, plus 240,000 years of audio. The tool is available through Google DeepMind. Marks are meant to stay readable after a crop or a filter, without changing what a person sees or hears. The release lines up with the EU AI Act, which requires generative platforms to make outputs identifiable to automated systems. Source: [independent.co.uk](https://www.independent.co.uk/bulletin/news/google-synthid-detector-ai-detection-tool-b3063389.html)

**AWS takes aim at runaway AI agent behavior with Strands Box: InfoWorld**
Amazon Web Services has put out Strands Box, an open-source sandbox that pairs operating-system isolation with policies on what an agent may do next, InfoWorld reports. It landed in developer preview on October 7 under the Apache 2.0 license, and it currently runs on Macs with Apple silicon on macOS 15 or later. The Dogwood policy language and its evaluation engine can use an agent's recorded activity across tools, so a file read through a shell can trigger limits on later network requests. In AWS's own example, an incident agent may post to a Slack channel no more than three times every 10 minutes, and Box enforces the cap. Checks cover the shell, Python interpreters, and the Model Context Protocol broker; the network gateway can attach credentials to approved requests without showing those secrets to the agent. Pareekh Jain, CEO of Pareekh Consulting, said the underlying technologies are not new and that the gain is consistent enforcement across agent frameworks. Files opened through a harness's own tools stay under operating-system limits and are not scored by Dogwood. Source: [infoworld.com](https://www.infoworld.com/article/4232439/aws-takes-aim-at-runaway-ai-agent-behavior-with-strands-box.html)

Meta on October 7 added AI checks to ad review aimed at ads that look harmless and then send people to prohibited material off the platform, ContentGrip reports. ### The Thread: Eight hundred developers, still a human in the loop
Nearly 800 software developers filed into a San Francisco hall last week for a conference hosted by Modal, and the argument on stage is a split that now runs across the seven. Scott Wu, whose coding-agent startup Cognition reached a $48 billion valuation last month, told them to be ambitious: virtual employees that work on outcomes instead of tasks. His turning point, he said, was the AIME moment last year, when models began outperforming humans on the high-level math contests he used to enter. His account was that large language models today are optimized for assistance with reinforcement learning from human feedback, so they are trained to please a person in the loop and fail at unattended work. Cat Wu, head of product for Claude Code at Anthropic, put a ratio on the stall: the model does 80 percent of the work, a human still does 20 percent, and that 20 percent repeats. Dax Raad, who built OpenCode, said the failure he is fighting is human — engineers not paying enough attention to code the models write. Microsoft on Wednesday unveiled its latest effort to run AI in Windows PCs rather than in the cloud, which the company said would bring costs down for customers. Anjney Midha, a former general partner at Andreessen Horowitz, and former executives at Google, Apple, and Nvidia have launched a company aimed at making that compute easier and more affordable for smaller companies and startups. More than 100 data-center moratoriums are being considered across the United States, and that count is now a cloud-build problem, not only a zoning story. AWS chief executive Matt Garman, in a blog post reported by IT Pro, said the build-out is so important geopolitically that there are widespread reports of various countries intentionally seeding misinformation in the US about data centers to trick the country into slowing down. He set Amazon next to Microsoft on process: like Microsoft, he said, the company has stopped using nondisclosure agreements when seeking approval from government agencies, is providing information as early as possible, and is listening to concerns. On the resource claims, he said US golf courses alone use around 200 times as much water as all of Amazon's data centers put together. He also said the sites are not driving up energy prices and are not emitting huge amounts of pollution via large backup diesel generators. The local case he offered is tax revenue, positive economic impact, large numbers of good jobs, education programs, and other benefits, plus thousands of construction jobs that he said benefit families and local small businesses. # MAG 7 Daily
> **Amazon pledged more than one billion dollars to the towns hosting its data centers.**

**What You Need to Know:** Amazon pledged more than one billion dollars over five years to U.S. towns that host its data centers, funding schools, training, and energy and water work as local moratoriums pile up. Google put four of its AI chips on a prototype satellite. Prosecutors charged a California man over restricted Nvidia servers bound for China, and New Mexico is seeking as much as forty billion dollars from Meta after a privacy trial.

### Top News
**Amazon pledges more than $1 billion to data-center towns: GeekWire**
Amazon Web Services said Friday it will spend more than $1 billion over five years in U.S. communities where it operates data centers, in a program GeekWire reports is called Built Together. The money targets local priorities including education, job training, energy affordability, and water and energy preservation; GeekWire adds free community college and energy upgrades for homes and schools, on top of more than $1 billion Amazon says it has already given those communities over the past three years. Amazon said it invested $276 billion in data centers between 2011 and 2025, with major projects and expansions in Indiana, Louisiana, North Carolina, Virginia, and Mississippi. AWS chief executive Matt Garman said more than 100 data-center moratoriums are being considered, and that “the countries that lead in AI will shape it and get the most from it.” Amazon also said it will stop using nondisclosure agreements with government agencies on data-center projects, install lower-emission backup generators at new sites, publish its energy and water use each year, and pay enough for power to keep local electricity bills from rising. AWS pledged to be water positive across its data centers by 2030, meaning it aims to return more water than it uses, and said it has already reached 75 percent of the progress toward that target. Source: [geekwire.com](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/amazon-pledges-1b-to-data-center-communities-warns-that-local-opposition-threatens-u-s-ai-lead/) https://www.arise.tv/amazon-aws-to-invest-over-1bn-in-us-communities-over-five-years/ https://finimize.com/content/aws-pledges-1-billion-to-ease-data-center-pushback

**Google flies four TPUs on a Project Suncatcher prototype: Google**
Google said it launched a prototype satellite carrying four TPUs into orbit with Planet, on SpaceX’s Transporter-18 rideshare. The flight is the first step of Project Suncatcher, a research effort to see whether scalable machine-learning infrastructure can one day run in space. Over the coming weeks Google will collect in-orbit data on how the chips handle physical stress, radiation, and thermal extremes, and use whatever it learns to refine later designs. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/Google/status/2105803583648100611) https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/google-project-suncatcher-facts/?utm_source=tw&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=og

### The Counterpoint
**The community check is about a tenth of a percent of this year’s build: GeekWire**
GeekWire’s arithmetic is the hard cut against the pledge. The additional $1 billion over five years works out to about $200 million a year, or about one-tenth of 1 percent of the roughly $220 billion in capital expenses Amazon is projecting this year, largely on data centers and chips — spending GeekWire says is more than the cash the business generates annually. The same report says Microsoft and Google are spending on a similar scale, and that local opposition has become a real limit on the AI buildout. A fund that small does not change the size of the build Garman says moratoriums could stall. ### The Thread: Campuses still rising, chips leaving the books
Across five operators, TrendForce’s October tracker finds that most of the capacity it can size is already under construction on the remaining path to 2030, and it reports AWS holding the most gigawatts under construction while Google’s build goes global. The tracker follows major hyperscalers in the United States and China and monitors nearly 2,000 facilities, checking satellite imagery, permit filings, and utility records against its own supply-chain research. Each bar is an operator’s remaining path to a 2030 pipeline target after capacity already online is stripped out: active construction, permitted or planned sites that already have a power figure, and pipeline that has reached neither stage. Permitted or planned sites that cannot yet be sized in megawatts are excluded, so the planned band understates the true total. The count includes self-built campuses, build-to-suit developments, and fully leased colocation, and it excludes shared colocation, cloud regions, and power offtake agreements. Booked delays and unstaged capacity are only a small share of that 2030 window, and where they appear they attach to a few named sites rather than the fleet. Off that construction map, Bloomberg says the Financial Times reported Amazon is exploring a deal to shift about $8 billion of top-end Nvidia chips off its balance sheet. On September 30, Synopsys used its 2026 Investor Day in New York to announce multi-year agreements with OpenAI and with Amazon Web Services, and it issued fiscal 2027 revenue and profit forecasts that came in above analysts’ expectations. Design Automation, the segment that holds its chip-design software and Ansys simulation products, made $5.3 billion, or 75 percent of revenue, in fiscal 2025, grew 25.6 percent that year, helped by the Ansys purchase, and earned a 41.8 percent operating margin. In August, management had raised its fiscal 2026 revenue guide to $9.69 billion to $9.74 billion and reported more than 30 active customer engagements for its agentic AI platform, including one agent that can run a whole chip verification cycle on its own. Yahoo Finance calculates that if those AI tools added a tenth to Design Automation revenue, the gain would be about $530 million a year, roughly 7.5 percent of fiscal 2025 revenue. > **Two new Nvidia tools shut down AI agents that break the rules.**

**What You Need to Know:** Nvidia shipped two tools meant to shut down AI agents that break the rules. OpenShell restricts what an agent can do from the CPU, and Sentry watches from networking hardware, apart from the chips running the agent. Anthropic is tying cloud-managed agents to OpenShell, with Microsoft on the partner list.

### Top News
**Nvidia unveils a platform to keep AI agents inside limits: Benzinga**
Nvidia introduced OpenShell, software that runs on central processors and restricts what an AI agent can do. It also launched Sentry, a monitoring layer on networking hardware, separate from the CPUs and GPUs running the agents. The software is partly open source and is positioned as a reference design that partners are expected to turn into products. Named partners include Cisco, Microsoft, Oracle, CoreWeave, Dell, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Lenovo, Arm, and Intel. Nvidia is partnering with Anthropic to integrate cloud-managed agents with OpenShell. Chief executive Jensen Huang said AI’s potential depends on addressing safety challenges, called for faster advances in AI safety alongside AI capabilities, and said the platform is meant to bring industry, researchers, and public-sector groups together to share best practices, align on evaluations, and strengthen international cooperation. Source: [benzinga.com](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/tech/26/09/62016478/nvidia-unveils-ai-safety-platform-to-keep-ai-agents-under-control-partners-with-anthropic)

> **Four Copilot pillars turn Microsoft's work software into an agent layer.**

**What You Need to Know:** Microsoft's largest Copilot update, announced on 25 September, is the same shift: Satya Nadella is pitching Copilot as a new operating system for work, built from Autopilot, Code, Home and Office. Home and Code start through the Frontier programme in the coming weeks. A later private-preview clock covers Autopilot and a new Today view.

### Top News
**Microsoft's largest Copilot update adds Home, Code and Autopilot: Dealroom**
Satya Nadella announced the largest Microsoft Copilot update to date on 25 September 2026 and called Copilot "a new OS for work" spanning every model, form factor and task. Autopilot is a proactive, long-running agent for the enterprise. Code lets people build apps with Copilot hosted inside the company tenant, on the same underlying technology as GitHub Copilot. Home merges Chat and Cowork into one starting point, and Office puts Word, Excel and PowerPoint fully inside Copilot. Copilot can be invoked in Teams. Today is a proactive view that surfaces the most important information across Microsoft 365. Microsoft says Home and Code begin rolling out through its Frontier programme in the coming weeks, Autopilot expands to private preview at the end of September, and Today enters private preview in October, later coming to Outlook and Teams. Source: [app.dealroom.co](https://app.dealroom.co/news/note/microsoft-unveils-its-biggest-copilot-update-home-code-and-autopilot)

**DeepMind's chief says Gemini 4 should land well before year-end: Trending Topics**
Post-training on Gemini 4 was already in view; what changed is the clock. Sundar Pichai describes Gemini 4 as a "significantly larger" frontier model focused on coding and autonomous AI agents. In July, DeepMind started what it called its "most ambitious pre-training run yet." Gemini 3.5 Pro, originally announced for I/O in May, never shipped, reportedly because its coding performance fell short. Google instead released cheaper Flash models, Gemini 3.7 Flash in August and Gemini 3.8 Flash in early September. The last true flagship, Gemini 3 Pro, dates to November 2025. TestingCatalog reports Google has been testing Gemini 4 Pro checkpoints under the code name Argon since mid-September; those leaks say a response can run to 256,000 tokens, four times the previous limit, and that the highest reasoning mode took 2.4 to 20 minutes an answer. Source: [trendingtopics.eu](https://www.trendingtopics.eu/gemini-4-rumors-google/)

The lead treats Copilot as a new operating system for work. Ars Technica is the dispatch that puts two of the seven in one frame. Musk has insisted investors think of Tesla as a robotics and autonomous-vehicle company, and he has targeted a $20 trillion valuation, nearly four times the value Ars assigns to Nvidia as market leader. The piece sets a physical limit next to that figure: charging gaps still limit electric trucking as the 500-mile truck moves into volume production. The cross-company fact is not a shared chip order or a joint filing. It is a valuation premise measured against Nvidia, spoken by a chief executive who did not attend his own production launch. > **Six hundred forty-four million dollars in premiums did not get Tesla Insurance into New York.**

**What You Need to Know:** New York rejected Tesla General Insurance’s plan to cover only Tesla vehicles, after the company’s insurance entities reported $644.2 million in direct written premiums in the first half of 2026. Google is putting Gemini on the phone for ordinary business calls and giving enterprise Gemini Live a lip-synced face. Forty-two state attorneys general are lining up consumer-protection rules for Meta’s chatbots, and a Washington filing lists 277 Microsoft cuts in the Seattle region.

### Top News
**New York blocks Tesla’s VIN-only auto filing: InsuranceNewsNet**
The New York Department of Financial Services rejected a filing from Tesla General Insurance Inc. that would have limited eligibility to Tesla vehicles identified by vehicle identification number. Regulators raised concerns under Section 2324 of New York Insurance Law before reviewing the filing’s actuarial merits, according to an analysis from S&P Global Market Intelligence. Tesla’s insurance entities generated $644.2 million in direct written premiums in the first half of 2026: California $477.8 million, Texas $60.4 million, Nevada $23.3 million, and Maryland $15 million. New York produced no direct written premium in that period even though Tesla Insurance Co. is licensed in the state, S&P said. Source: [insurancenewsnet.com](https://insurancenewsnet.com/innarticle/tesla-insurance-blocked-as-ny-regulators-examine-connected-car-coverage)

**Gemini will place the business call, then stay on the line: Notebookcheck**
Google is rolling out “Call for me” as an early preview on Pixel 11, initially only in the United States, so Gemini handles the conversation rather than only dialing. The support page lists product-availability checks, quote requests, reservations, phone menus, and time on hold. Emergency calls, marketing calls, and payments are excluded, and credit card numbers, passwords, and health information must not be shared. Before the call, the app shows the number and the information Gemini will give or request; Gemini then identifies itself as the user’s AI assistant and says the call is recorded. Users can follow a live transcript, listen in, or take over, and afterward get a summary. Notebookcheck reports that transcripts are stored on Google’s servers, audio stays on the device, and neither is used to train Google’s models. The feature is separate from Agentic Calling, which since 2025 has placed certain business calls from Search or AI Mode rather than free-form tasks in the Gemini app. Source: [notebookcheck.net](https://www.notebookcheck.net/Google-puts-Gemini-on-the-phone-AI-handles-calls-for-questions-and-reservations.1408327.0.html)

**Forty-two states move to police Meta’s chatbots and agents: simplywall.st**
Meta is facing a multistate push in which 42 state attorneys general are coordinating oversight of its AI systems. The coalition aims to enforce safeguards for chatbots and AI agents through state consumer-protection and civil-rights laws. That would extend scrutiny beyond existing federal oversight into state enforcement. Source: [simplywall.st](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/media/nasdaq-meta/meta-platforms/news/meta-platforms-meta-draws-42-state-push-to-police-ai-chatbot)

**A state filing lists 277 Microsoft cuts in the Seattle region: GeekWire**
A Washington state filing lists 277 positions Microsoft eliminated in the Seattle region, one job title at a time. Art, game production, game design, technical art, and audio design account for 77 of them. Software engineering is the largest single category, at 60. Source: [geekwire.com](https://www.geekwire.com/2026/artists-game-designers-and-producers-hit-hard-as-microsoft-cuts-277-jobs-in-washington-state/)

**Apple and Qualcomm renew a global patent license: 9to5Mac**
Qualcomm and Apple have renewed their global patent licensing agreement. The renewed deal extends a license that had been set to expire in 2027. Source: [9to5mac.com](https://9to5mac.com/2026/09/24/apple-and-qualcomm-renew-global-patent-licensing-agreement/)

### Company Desk
**Gemini 3.8 Live grows a face that lip-syncs and keeps talking: Digital Trends**
A week after Google launched Gemini 3.8 Live and Live Extended Thinking on September 15, Live Avatar adds near real-time generated video so the agent can lip-sync, use facial expressions, and answer without a freeze between turns. Google is keeping the feature inside Gemini Enterprise for now, for uses such as customer service and interactive walkthroughs, with 97 languages and speech, lip movements, and expressions that adjust without restarting the conversation. Preset avatars are available, and approved enterprise customers can build custom ones from a reference image that preserve likeness, style, or character identity. The avatar can still call tools and fetch information in the background. Generated audio and video carry SynthID watermarking. TechRadar reported that Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking outperformed GPT-Live-1 Astra and Grok Voice Think Fast 2.0 across multiple benchmarks while remaining cheaper to run per hour of input audio. Source: [digitaltrends.com](https://www.digitaltrends.com/computing/google-has-given-gemini-3-8-live-a-face-that-can-lip-sync-react-and-use-tools-in-the-background/)

**Golden Gate drops Intel Macs, Boot Camp, and AFP: MacRumors**
macOS Golden Gate is the first macOS that runs only on Apple silicon; Intel Macs cannot run it and stay on macOS Tahoe. Boot Camp Assistant is unsupported. There is no AFP client, Time Capsule no longer works with Golden Gate Macs, and AirPort Utility is no longer included in the install. Upgrading removes Rosetta 2, though it can be reinstalled if an installed app needs it, and Golden Gate is the last macOS with full Rosetta support. A warning appears when a Rosetta app runs, and affected apps are listed under Settings, General, About, Intel-Based Apps. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/09/24/macos-golden-gate-features-removed/)

**Suing lawyers say Meta stamped privilege on too much: The Verge**
In ongoing lawsuits over alleged harm to teens’ safety and mental health, Meta’s lawyers have argued that certain evidence should be withheld as attorney-client privilege. Lawyers suing the company said this week that the label has been applied far too broadly. They pointed to a recently unsealed document, and The Verge reported that employees ordered “attorney/client privilege” hats while those child-safety disclosures were being fought. Source: [theverge.com](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1000370/meta-instagram-attorney-client-privilege-hats)

**Microsoft drops the Copilot Plus PC name: The Verge**
About two and a half years after Microsoft pushed “Copilot Plus PCs” as the machines with enough on-device AI, The Verge reports that Microsoft is killing off the brand. Windows Central’s Zac Bowden is the reporter The Verge cites. The Verge writes that Microsoft and Qualcomm seem to be admitting the brand is already dead. Source: [theverge.com](https://www.theverge.com/tech/1000495/microsoft-is-killing-off-the-copilot-plus-pc-brand)

### The Counterpoint
**The book grew, and it was never built for a broad market: InsuranceNewsNet**
The New York block lands on a business S&P measured as still expanding, and on a product its own analyst says is not a broad-market insurer. Previous S&P research found Tesla generated $1.37 billion in direct written premiums in 2025, up 40.7% from $970.8 million a year earlier. Tesla-affiliated insurers wrote 75.9% of that business directly in 2025, compared with 32.6% in 2024. California remained the largest market, nearly 70% of 2025 premium volume, at $725 million. Tim Zawacki, head of financial institutions research at S&P Global Market Intelligence, said the purpose “is not to be a competitive source of insurance coverage for a broad segment of the market” and is “to essentially eliminate a point of friction in the Tesla sales process.” He said the shift into affiliated carriers emerged partly because some insurers were reluctant to write electric-vehicle business or charged more because of repair costs and loss severity. Source: [insurancenewsnet.com](https://insurancenewsnet.com/innarticle/tesla-insurance-blocked-as-ny-regulators-examine-connected-car-coverage)

### The Thread: Ten billion dollars on a chip still years out
DensityAI, founded a year ago by former leaders of Tesla’s Dojo supercomputer program, is in advanced talks to raise hundreds of millions of dollars in a round that would value it at $10 billion, The Information reported, citing two people with knowledge of the discussions. The valuation is high for a company whose chips those people described as early in development and potentially years from mass production. The company’s leaders have told potential investors they have an agreement in which Amazon Web Services would purchase eventual chips from DensityAI if the chips meet certain performance requirements, the people said. The buy, as those investors were told it, is conditional on performance.

Elon Musk said Colossus 2, an AI computing cluster built by his xAI business, may more than double its current Nvidia chip count by the end of the year, Bloomberg reported. That is a volume target on chips already in the cluster, set against a startup valuation on chips that are still early. They share a calendar. DensityAI’s founders left Tesla’s Dojo effort a year ago and are now describing an Amazon purchase that triggers only if performance requirements are met, while the chips remain years from mass production. Musk’s year-end aim sits on Nvidia parts Colossus 2 already uses, and the scale he named is more than double that current count. For Amazon, the DensityAI clause is optional supply if a new chip qualifies. For Nvidia, Colossus 2 is demand on the parts shipping now. Tesla’s name in the account is the Dojo program those founders left, not the buyer. Source: [theinformation.com](https://www.theinformation.com/articles/startup-founded-ex-tesla-dojo-leaders-nears-10-billion-valuation)

# MAG 7 Daily
> **Hundreds of thousands of merchants can now offer Prime on their own sites at no extra cost.**

**What You Need to Know:** Hundreds of thousands of merchants on Amazon’s U.S. fulfillment network can now turn on fast, free Prime delivery on their own websites at no added cost to them or their shoppers. Google is rolling Gemini audio models out to developers the same day its DeepMind chief says Gemini 4 is in refinement. Apple priced a two-phone number handoff, and Meta put a pocket Muse device and a hundred-gram headset on a launch path.

### Top News
**Merchants switch on Prime delivery on their own sites: About Amazon**
Merchants using Amazon Multichannel Fulfillment in the U.S. can now offer fast, free Prime delivery on their own websites at no additional cost to them or their shoppers. Hundreds of thousands of merchants can activate it in minutes, with no changes to checkout, payments, or store policies. Through the new MCF Preferred Pricing Program, merchants can save up to 25% on fulfillment fees across their own websites, marketplaces, and social channels, with no contracts required. Source: [aboutamazon.com](https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/retail/amazon-mcf-prime-delivery-merchant-websites?utm_source=rss)

**Gemini Audio models roll out to Studio, Notebook, and the API: Google**
Google said new Gemini Audio models are rolling out across Google AI Studio, Gemini Notebook, and the Gemini API. The linked post is titled around Gemini 3.8 text-to-speech. Google said the models are coming soon to Google Vids and Gemini Enterprise. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/Google/status/2102781492644413566)

**iPhone Handoff gets a monthly price and a short carrier list: MacRumors**
iPhone Handoff in iOS 27 lets the same number sit on two iPhones, active on only one at a time, and it is separate from the existing Handoff that continues an app on another Apple device. Calls, voicemail, messages — including iMessage, RCS, SMS, and MMS — and Find My location move to the phone that is unlocked, with a “Switched to this iPhone” confirmation. T-Mobile in the United States is charging customers 5 per month; Deutsche Telekom is charging €6.95 per month, but only on plans that do not already include multi-SIM, while MagentaMobil L includes one multi-SIM and XL includes two. The feature is available through T-Mobile and Telekom; Verizon and EE will support it later this year, and AT&T has not committed, with a spokesperson pointing to existing eSIM activation and transfer options. Both phones need iOS 27 or later, Wi-Fi, the same Apple Account, Messages in iCloud, and FaceTime and iMessage on that account. Stopping the service means contacting the carrier; deleting an eSIM may not stop the charge. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/guide/iphone-handoff-how-it-works-carrier-support-cost/)

**DeepMind chief says Gemini 4 is in refinement: The Verge**
Koray Kavukcuoglu, in his first media appearance as leader of Google’s DeepMind division, told The Information that Gemini 4 is in its refinement stage. The Verge reports Google is nearing the launch after trailing rival developers on flagship AI releases. Source: [theverge.com](https://www.theverge.com/tech/999802/google-deepmind-gemini-4-timeline-koray-kavukcuoglu)

**Apple sets an early-next-week fix for iPhone 18 Pro reboots: 9to5Mac**
Apple confirmed to 9to5Mac that a software update is coming early next week for iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max phones that freeze and reboot after a failed Face ID attempt. 9to5Mac had reported the failures on Monday and read them as a software glitch rather than a hardware fault. Source: [9to5mac.com](https://9to5mac.com/2026/09/23/apple-iphone-18-pro-rebooting-bug-software-update-fix/)

### Company Desk
**Muse stays free and adds Walmart, Sephora, and Best Buy shopping: Benzinga**
After Meta’s test of a human concierge for Muse, Benzinga reports Muse stays free and adds shopping with Walmart, Sephora, and Best Buy. The shopping additions are the new commercial step on the agent. Source: [benzinga.com](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/tech/26/09/61963074/mark-zuckerberg-muse-free-walmart-sephora-best-buy-ai-shopping)

**AI factories come online as Egypt’s institute participation grows: NVIDIA Newsroom**
NVIDIA said AI factories are coming online across Africa, giving developers and startups more local computing. More than 85,000 developers across the continent have trained through the NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute, and participation in Egypt grew more than 10x in one year. NVIDIA pointed to Egypt startups using that talent and infrastructure in Arabic speech, healthcare, robotics, and financial services. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/nvidianewsroom/status/2102714202544611351)

### The Thread: A hundred-gram headset against a shelved pendant
A hundred grams is the weight MacRumors gives Meta’s new VR glasses, five times lighter than the Meta Quest 3, with full-color passthrough and a 5K display. The same report says Apple has shelved plans to launch an AI pendant, while Mark Zuckerberg used a “one more thing” slot at Connect to unveil Muse Charm, a puck about the size of an Apple Watch with a tamagotchi-like avatar for talking to Muse. Zuckerberg said Meta packed the real-time voice and avatar stack into something that fits on a keychain, started by a tap on a fingerprint sensor in the corner, without unlocking a phone or opening an app, and that Charm is aimed at sale by the holiday season, with more to share later this year. The VR glasses are set to launch in the spring at a starting price of 1,300. Meta says they offer cinema-grade clarity with Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos, up to three hours of continuous high-resolution media playback on a single charge, every game available for Quest headsets, Xbox Cloud Gaming, and a virtual keyboard and trackpad on a desk when connected to a PC or Mac. For context, MacRumors notes an M5 Apple Vision Pro weighs 750–800 grams depending on configuration. An audio-only Ray-Ban model, presented against the “pervert glasses” label, supports media playback and calls and runs for up to 12 hours, while the charging case adds up to 48 hours. The refreshed camera Ray-Ban Meta is slimmer, adds a button that activates Meta AI, and is said to have nine hours of battery versus eight on the second-generation model, plus a six-microphone array Meta says can cut out over 90 percent of background noise. The 12MP camera supports 3K video, with Dolby Atmos spatial audio support coming soon, and prices start at 449. An FDA-cleared hearing enhancement is due later this year, as part of a Meta One subscription or a one-time cost of 149, with a 30-day free trial. Source: [macrumors.com](https://www.macrumors.com/2026/09/24/meta-did-a-one-more-thing-and-its-an-ai-tamagotchi/)

**U.S. government urges Supreme Court to reverse Apple contempt ruling over App Store commission:** 9to5Mac
The U.S. government and several legal and business groups filed briefs with the Supreme Court urging reversal of at least part of the civil contempt ruling against Apple in the Epic Games lawsuit. The district court held Apple in contempt after the company allowed external purchase links yet imposed a 27 percent commission on those transactions. Apple has since removed the commission entirely. The company maintains that the original injunction text did not prohibit charging a commission and that lower courts improperly relied on the spirit of the order rather than its wording. The injunction states that Apple is permanently restrained from prohibiting developers from including buttons, external links or other calls to action that direct customers to purchasing mechanisms outside In-App Purchasing. The Supreme Court agreed in late June to hear Apple’s argument on this point. **Google and the Gates Foundation to bring AI resources to 200 million farmers across the Global South.:** Google Blog
Google partnered with the Gates Foundation to direct $100 million toward organizations that scale AI-powered climate and crop insights. The program targets 200 million smallholder farmers in Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia, an increase from the current 50 million reached. Smallholder farmers produce nearly 35 percent of the world’s food across more than 500 million farms yet often lack access to satellite data, financial services and public support needed for unpredictable weather. The combined funding includes dedicated technical support from Google researchers to deploy real-time climate, agricultural and language AI tools. Source: [blog.google](https://blog.google/company-news/outreach-and-initiatives/google-org/partnering-with-the-gates-foundation-to-bring-ai-resources-to-200-million-farmers-across-the-global-south/)

The Google-Gates partnership adds dedicated technical support from Google researchers for real-time tools. Microsoft’s discount structure requires customers to commit to additional payments based on usage of certain features. Amazon’s service targets workloads that involve generative AI agents. Meta’s concierge test focuses on its newest agent product. The combined activity illustrates parallel efforts to extend AI capabilities with measurable scale targets and pricing adjustments.
